builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
summary: TASK memory replaces text-only retrieval (BM25/vector RAG) with a triple store: a text note holding content, a removable knowledge edit serving as an in-model address keyed by subject, and a pair of content-free steering vectors that decide per query whether the model adopts the memory or its parametric answer. It costs the engineering of a knowledge-editing pipeline (e.g., rank-one edits) plus activation-steering infrastructure, requires access to model internals (ruling out API-only models), and adds steering and editing overhead per memory write and per query. It can fail through editing side effects (the paper reports up to 49% memory-misapplication when retrieval is combined with weight editing), degraded behavior on models or domains outside the four tested families, and residual version confusion when superseded facts remain stored.
rationale: The method runs on frozen open models in the 8B-27B range and reports strong hallucination reductions, but it requires per-model steering vectors and knowledge edits plus per-query gating, so its gains must be validated on the reader's own memory workload before production adoption.

claims.statement: TASK memory replaces text-only retrieval (BM25/vector RAG) with a triple store: a text note holding content, a removable knowledge edit serving as an in-model address keyed by subject, and a pair of content-free steering vectors that decide per query whether the model adopts the memory or its parametric answer. It costs the engineering of a knowledge-editing pipeline (e.g., rank-one edits) plus activation-steering infrastructure, requires access to model internals (ruling out API-only models), and adds steering and editing overhead per memory write and per query. It can fail through editing side effects (the paper reports up to 49% memory-misapplication when retrieval is combined with weight editing), degraded behavior on models or domains outside the four tested families, and residual version confusion when superseded facts remain stored.

Reduces memory-ignoring hallucinations to at most 1.5% across ten model-dataset cells; cuts neighbour misuse from 39.2% to 7.5%; +16.4 pp over BM25 RAG on a 300-memory library (holding at 3,000 memories); +7.5 pp multi-hop accuracy on MQuAKE.
